title: The Index: kills-archive.json
description: Every kill still standing, from every sweep the machine has run. kills.json is THIS sweep and must stay this sweep, because stats.killed counts it and the site holds the two to the same number. This file is the record behind the kill list's own promise that a kill is kept. It is rebuilt whole from the machine's append-only archive every night, so it carries no state of its own and cannot drift from what was recorded. Observations only, exactly as in kills.json: no field here may carry a claim about why a company did anything.

swept_at_utc.description: The sweep that rebuilt this file. It matches stats.json exactly: the file spans every sweep, but it was written by one of them, and two clocks in one export is the thing this repository refuses.

archive_since.description: The day the record begins: the first sweep in the machine's archive. A date and not a count, because this site has no sweep number and must not grow one.

by_rule.description: Every live rule reports, including the ones that have never fired. A rule missing from a summary reads as a rule that was never run.

retired_skipped.description: Kill events in the archive that fired a rule since retired. They are counted and not published: the events stay in the append-only archive because it records what the machine did, and editing it would be worse than the finding it holds.

vacated.description: Records explicitly withdrawn by a kill_vacated event. A kill is a dated observation and stays true when a posting reappears, so nothing is withdrawn automatically: a row leaves this file only by a deliberate act with a reason attached.

kills.description: May be empty. An empty record is the best history the machine can have.

id.description: A digest of the posting URL and the rule that fired, and of nothing else. The same posting killed by the same rule is one record no matter which pipeline found it, how many nights it fired, or how often this file has been rebuilt.

slug.description: The card URL. Assigned across the whole record at once, so a base more than one posting claims gives every claimant the suffixed form: the slug depends on the set and never on the order it was read in, because a slug that shifted when an older kill joined would break a card somebody had already shared.

kill_rule.description: Never null here. A record with no live rule is not published, so it never reaches this file; 'evergreen' is absent for the same reason it is absent from kills.schema.json.

first_killed_at_utc.description: The instant of the sweep that first found it.

times_fired.description: How many sweeps have seen this rule fire on this posting. One finding observed repeatedly is one record, not several, so the count lives on the row rather than becoming extra rows.

pipeline.description: Which machine found it. The deep verified sweep, or the wide crawl. The rule and the identity are the same either way; this only records who was looking.
